questions: Does the oval return to near 100% finishes at about 1.65 s with 0.12 m track and 0.03 m radius, confirming that the drivetrain change caused the regression?
On the s-bend and slalom, at which track position does the first off-track or line-loss event occur, and are the outer sensors reading near 1 or near 0 at that step?
Does the 0.5 kg mass cause more steering oscillation than the 0.6 kg baseline on the oval?

intent: Test whether the wider ±0.032 m array alone improves the s-bend and slalom, with the drivetrain restored to the baseline wheel track and radius that gave the stable oval. I expect the oval to finish again at about 1.65 s with low steering oscillation, and the s-bend and slalom progress to exceed the baseline's 0.17 and 0.12. Completion on those two tracks is not expected yet.
learning: Iteration 1 showed that the wider array is not enough by itself and that the narrower 0.10 m track with the larger wheel radius hurt the oval. This iteration isolates the array from the drivetrain. If the s-bend and slalom still go off track with the wider array and a baseline drivetrain, the next geometry lever is the sensor lead (y) or the sensor footprint size, not the spread.
rationale: Iteration 1 changed three things at once: a wider array (±0.032 m), a narrower wheel track (0.12 to 0.10 m), and a lighter, larger-radius drivetrain (0.5 kg, 0.033 m). The score fell from 356.6 to 341.7. The oval went from 20/20 finishes to 17/20, mean time slowed from 1.65 s to 1.84 s, and oval steering oscillation rose from 0.15 to 0.26. The s-bend and slalom improved only a little (progress 0.17 to 0.24 and 0.12 to 0.19), and both still end off track. The wider array helped the bends somewhat, but the narrower track and changed drivetrain seem to have destabilised the oval. The slalom also gained a line-loss event. This points at the track width and drivetrain as the likely cause of the oval regression, and the array as the partial gain on the bends. Next I keep the wider array, which is the change with evidence behind it, and restore the baseline wheel track (0.12 m) and wheel radius (0.03 m) to recover oval stability and speed. Mass stays at 0.5 kg so that the array and the drivetrain are tested separately. I expect the oval to return to near-complete finishes (about 1.65 s), and the s-bend and slalom to progress further than the baseline, though they may still go off track. The sensor footprint stays at 12 mm.
